summary.text: 用 means ‘use’ or ‘put into effect.’ One paleographic interpretation reads its ancient graph as a handled container; the proposal that it was borrowed for a word with a similar sound cannot be verified because the container’s spoken name is unknown.

formation.text: Disputed. One account treats the whole graph as a pictograph of a container, with its body on the left and handle on the right. The received 說文 analysis instead parses it as 卜 plus 中. Other accounts relate 用 and 同 as graphic variants or a divided graph, or analyze 用 as 同 with a handle added and 同 as phonetic. The inspected evidence does not settle these competing analyses or establish an internal phonetic component.

components.text: The entire graph is interpreted as a handled bucket or container: the left side is its body and the right its handle. This is an attributed paleographic interpretation; no inscription image was independently checked here.

history.text: A character-form catalogue indexes oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, seal-script and 說文 forms, but its text does not describe individual strokes or establish a detailed sequence of shape changes.

The bucket-and-handle interpretation differs from the received 說文 parsing 從卜從中. A separate account relates 用 and 同 as graphic variants or a divided graph; another describes 用 as 同 with a handle added and assigns 同 a sound role. These analyses remain unresolved.

uncertainties.text: The proposed borrowing from a container picture to ‘put into effect/use’ cannot be tested phonetically: the depicted object’s spoken name is not known. 用’s own reconstructed readings do not establish that missing name or a sound match.

Oracle-bone examples attest 用 in contexts indicating whether a proposed action was carried out, but the first occurrence and relative chronology of this use and the proposed container sense are unsettled. A Qin-slip container or measure use read 桶 does not determine their order.

senses.text: 用/不用 is reported after divination statements to indicate whether a proposed action was carried out. This attested use does not establish the graph’s original meaning.
One Qin-slip context is read 桶, ‘container’ or ‘measure.’ It preserves a container-related use but does not establish the graph’s original meaning or when this use arose.

senses.gloss: preposition equivalent to 以; sequential or causal conjunction
senses.text: Bronze-inscription examples include prepositional and conjunctive uses alongside the verb ‘use.’ The examples do not establish their relative chronology or development.
用 has the current meaning ‘use’ or ‘employ.’ The evidence does not establish a complete path from the attested inscriptional uses to its present range.

limitations.text: Several uses are attested, but the evidence does not establish a semantic development linking them. The proposed borrowing from a container picture to ‘carry out/use’ lacks a verifiable sound match because the pictured object’s spoken name is unknown.

overview.text: 用 means ‘use’ or ‘put into effect.’ One account sees its ancient graph as a handled container, borrowed for a word proposed to sound similar. The container’s spoken name is unknown, so that sound match cannot be verified.

components.text: The whole graph is interpreted as a handled container. Its proposed link to ‘use’ relies on sound similarity, but the container’s spoken name is unknown, so the match cannot be checked.
